Use this when Google won\'t let you sign in inside Yumeiro. You sign in on a normal browser and copy the cookie it got. It takes about two minutes on a computer.

Android may hold back background checks for hours on some phones. UnifiedPush lets a free push app wake Yumeiro on time, so new-episode and news alerts aren\'t late. No Google services, no account and no fees.
Install ntfy. It\'s free and open source. F-Droid has the build without Google services.
Or get ntfy from Google Play.
Open ntfy once and allow its notification. ntfy keeps one light connection open for every app that uses it.
In Android settings → Apps → ntfy → Battery, choose Unrestricted. Do the same for Yumeiro if your phone is on dontkillmyapp.com.
Come back here, turn on Reliable alerts and pick ntfy. Yumeiro gets a private push address.
Tap Send test. A wake-up should arrive within seconds and the status shows the time.
How it works: Yumeiro asks the ntfy server to wake it every few hours, using ntfy\'s free scheduled delivery. Each wake-up runs the normal checks, and nothing else is sent.
That\'s about 10 messages a day, far below ntfy.sh\'s free limit of 250. Nobody pays anything.
Wake-up messages carry no personal data, and Yumeiro ignores their text. Your list and history never leave the phone.
Running your own ntfy server? Set it as the default server in the ntfy app and Yumeiro uses it automatically.
Other UnifiedPush apps can be picked too, but only ntfy servers support the scheduled wake-ups.
